messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: feature request
parts:
I’m running stan.R and it’s great! But now I really really want it to do that thing where, after running 1/20 of the iterations, it prints an estimate of total runtime. Would it be possible to have this, without requiring some major programming efffort from the Stan team? I don’t want this to take time away from more important projects, but it would be super-helpful.
thx
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] feature request
parts:
Right now, that's being done in the interfaces, so the
issue tracker for RStan is where to make that request:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues

It's much better to put things there where they can be
tracked in one place than into e-mail where it'll get
lost.

It should actually be reasonably easy if the estimate is just assuming
the remaining iterations will take the same average time as the ones
that have happened. That'll almost certainly underestimate time after
10 iterations (the first few iterations are usually fast) and then
pretty quickly move to overestimating because warmup iterations are usually
slower.

We can roll it into a general feature for Stan 3 updates
on the C++ side. It all has to get pushed to and from
the interfaces, though, so it's a bit of work in how it'll
all be formatted, etc.

- Bob
